newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end steady.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end steady.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Tuesday's TIFFE day session flat after trading in a narrow three-tick range.

The key contract fell to an intraday low of 99.22 in early afternoon after Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama said the interest rate gap between Japan and other countries should be narrowed. However, its losses were later pared on short-covering. It settled at 99.24, unchanged from Monday.

Kajiyama told a parliamentary committee that Japan's interest rates on deposits were the lowest compared to other countries, with the exception of Switzerland, while rates on borrowing were high compared internationally.
He said: "As part of internationalisation component of the current reforms, we need to raise the low things and lower the high things."
His comments were interpreted by some players as suggesting Japan's interest rates should rise.
The impact on the Euroyen futures market, however, was short-lived, traders said.
"Selling did not last as people know that the current economic condition does not justify an interest rate hike," said a trust bank trader.
Traders said the December contract was likely to remain stuck between 99.20 and 99.25 in coming sessions unless stocks and bonds fluctuate wildly.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.50 percent, up from Monday's weighted average of 0.49 percent.
The BOJ drained a net 100 billion yen from the money market on Tuesday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
The overnight rate edged up as banks preferred to raise short-term funds rather than long-term funds, money traders said.
About 30 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.54 percent.
Two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent and one-month CDs were offered at 0.52 percent.
All CD rates were unchanged from Monday.
